subject: Azure co-sell: account atlas & consent orchestration
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Microsoft Partner Center <pc-ops@microsoft.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Account atlas & consent orchestration for Contoso

Hi PC team / Karthik,

Following up from last week's sync — Contoso is ready to move forward with Partner Center referrals for their initial 120 enterprise accounts. Two asks to get the intake and field handoff configured:

1) Ingestion SLA & account atlas: we will send a CSV with account IDs, MPNs, and primary contact. We need Partner Center to accept referrals in bulk and return a deterministically mapped seller owner within 48 hours so we can trigger field outreach.
2) Consent orchestration: Contoso requires explicit seller consent before a referral is locked to a field rep. We propose a DocuSign flow that returns a signed consent artifact to Redwood and Partner Center.

Attached: contoso_account_list.csv (sample), consent_template.docx.

Can you confirm the acceptable CSV schema and if PC can auto-assign a provisional seller during the 48h window? Karthik — tagging you for mapping rules (we should avoid duplicate ownership).

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: contoso_account_list.csv (csv), consent_template.docx (docx)

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@contoso.com>

Hi Olga — thanks for the note.

We can provide the full account list by EOD Pacific on Friday. A couple of constraints on our side:
- We cannot surface MPNs for a small subset of customers (privacy clause in our agreements).
- We require that the consent flow be auditable and stored for 7 years for compliance.

The DocuSign template you attached looks close. Can Redwood host a copy of the signed artifacts or do you need Microsoft to retain them? We prefer a single source of truth.

Best,
Sarah Lee
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Contoso

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Account atlas & consent orchestration for Contoso

Olga / team — quick proposal for the mapping rules so PC assignments avoid contention: 

Mapping rules (high level):
- Primary heuristic: match on Contoso CRM Account ID -> Partner Center account (exact)
- Fallback 1: match on domain + region if MPN absent
- Fallback 2: provisional owner = central Contoso seller pool (tagged fallback-provisional)
- Conflict resolution: if two sellers claim same account within 72h, escalate to internal arbitration queue (CS + Partnerships) and mark referral as "in-flight" so no double outreach occurs.

Operational items:
- We should compute an "ownership confidence" score and store it as a field in the intake CSV so PC can optionally prioritize assignments.
- I'll prepare mapping_rules_v1.pdf with the logic + examples.

Questions for PC: can you return an ownership_confidence float in the referral API? If not, we default to binary assignment.

-Karthik
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: mapping_rules_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Account atlas & consent orchestration for Contoso — field handshake

Vanessa / Neha — forwarding the thread. Key asks for field alignment: 

- We need a one-pager for field sellers that explains: how provisional ownership works, expected SLA to accept/decline referrals, and the consent artifact flow.
- Suggested next steps for a field play: 24h notification -> 48h acceptance window -> 7d nurture if unclaimed -> escalate to partner success.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Redwood sends CSV + mapping rules (Karthik) — by Fri 28 May
2) PC ingests and returns provisional owners + confidence scores — within 48h of ingestion
3) Contoso executes consent DocuSign; PC and Redwood receive signed artifact — within 5 business days
4) Field outreach begins after consent; Redwood hands off to assigned seller with a standardized handshake email.

Can you draft the seller one-pager and the handshake template? I can take the initial draft for the handshake email.

Thanks,
Olga

From: Microsoft Partner Center <pc-ops@microsoft.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@contoso.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Account atlas & consent orchestration for Contoso

Hi all — thanks for the clear MAP. A few notes from Partner Center ops: 

- CSV schema: we accept AccountID, AccountName, PrimaryContactEmail, Region, MPN (optional), ownership_confidence (optional). Sample ingestion endpoint: https://partner.microsoft.com/api/referrals/bulk
- We can return a provisional_owner_id and an ownership_confidence float (0.0-1.0) in the response JSON.
- DocuSign: we can act as a retention point for the signed consent if Contoso agrees; otherwise we will return a stored DocuSign link to Redwood and Contoso. We do not retain artifacts >7 years by default unless explicitly requested.
- SLA: bulk ingestion -> provisional owners returned within 48 business hours. Final lock happens after DocuSign callback.

Next steps:
1) Redwood to POST a 50-account pilot CSV to the ingestion endpoint (we'll use this to validate mapping rules).
2) Contoso to confirm retention preference for signed artifacts.
3) We'll provide a sample webhook schema for DocuSign callbacks by EOD Tuesday.

We'll kick off the pilot once the CSV is received.

Regards,
PC Ops (referrals team)
Microsoft Partner Center
